what: United Therapeutics develops treatments for pulmonary arterial hypertension, a rare disease of the lung arteries. It is also the leading company trying to make transplantable organs from genetically modified pigs.
customers: Pulmonologists, specialist hospitals and transplant centres, mostly in the United States.
money: Tyvaso, Remodulin and Orenitram for pulmonary hypertension
Unituxin for a childhood cancer and related products
moat: Decades of clinical data in a rare disease, with the inhaled Tyvaso delivery system and a specialist prescriber base that is small and well understood.
risks: Generic and competing versions of its main medicine are being approved
A single disease area produces almost all revenue
Organ manufacturing is scientifically ambitious and may never reach the market
opportunities: Operating margin of 47% and net margin of 42%, exceptional for a pharmaceutical company
No debt at all, with $2.1 billion of cash
Revenue grew about 11% last year and about 18% a year over three years
watch: Tyvaso revenue against generic competition, and organ transplant trial progress.
